---
title: "DataSHIELD naming (draft)"
description: "Checks a DataSHIELD client and server package against shared naming rules and renames what people approve."
---

::: {.callout-warning}
## Draft
The [rules](ds-naming-rules.qmd) aren't agreed with the DataSHIELD
developers yet, and may change. Both workflows have only been tested
locally, not yet in GitHub Actions or with a real Claude answer. This page
describes what exists today.
:::

Today the same kind of argument has many names across DataSHIELD packages,
e.g. `newobj` and `newobj.name`, or `df`, `data` and `dataName` for a data
frame. Two workflows bring a package in line with one set of
[naming rules](ds-naming-rules.qmd), in a breaking release:

- **`ds-naming-check.yml`** compares the package with the rules and
  proposes renames in a review pull request. It changes no code.
- **`ds-naming-apply.yml`** makes the renames people approved, in code,
  tests and documentation.

Both run from the **client** repository, which checks out its paired
server package, so client and server arguments change together. A package
without a counterpart can run them alone.

## How it works

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  check["Check: read the code,<br/>classify the arguments"] --> pr["Review PR with<br/>transformations.yml"]
  pr --> people["People approve<br/>or skip renames"]
  people -- "PR merged" --> apply["Apply: rename in code,<br/>tests and docs"]
  apply --> prs["One PR per repository"]
```

## The check

1. **Reads the package:** the user-facing functions (client: `NAMESPACE`
   exports; server: the Aggregate and Assign methods) with their arguments
   and documentation, and which client argument is passed to which server
   argument.
2. **Works out what each argument is:** its role (e.g. new object) or, for
   an object on the server, its class (e.g. data frame), from its name,
   default and documentation.
3. **Asks Claude about the unclear ones,** at most `max-claude-calls`
   functions per run. Claude only classifies; the name always comes from
   the rules. Answers are kept and reused until the argument's default or
   documentation changes.
4. **Proposes names by the rules,** distinct within a function, with client
   and server arguments in step.

The results go into a pull request on `bot-suggest/ds-naming/<branch>`:

- **`.github/ds-naming/transformations.yml`**: one entry per function and
  argument that would change or needs a decision;
- **`.github/ds-naming/report.md`**: the overview per package, plus what
  breaks the rules for package names, server methods, client and server
  calls, function names, argument order and test file names. Those are
  reported only; the apply workflow doesn't change them.

## Reviewing

Edit `transformations.yml` in the pull request. Each entry has a `status`:

| `status` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `proposed` | Waiting for a decision |
| `approved` | Rename it; you may change `proposed` first |
| `skip` | Keep the name |
| `unresolved` | The rules can't decide: fill in `proposed`, then approve or skip |
| `applied` | Done; kept as history |

Entries marked `rule_open: true` follow a rule that is still open. Your
decisions survive later checks. Merging the pull request starts the apply
workflow.

## The apply workflow

It checks each approved entry against the code first: an argument already
renamed is marked as applied, and a new name that is already taken is
reported as a conflict and not renamed. Then it renames, for each function:

- **R code** in `R/`, `tests/` and `vignettes/`, using R's parser: the
  argument, its uses in the function, and calls with `old = ` anywhere;
- **Roxygen blocks,** shared templates and `man/*.Rd`;
- **R chunks** in vignettes and the README.

Text is left alone: mentions of the old name in error messages are listed
for a person, and vignette prose isn't changed. A file that wouldn't parse
afterwards isn't changed either.

Each repository gets one pull request, on
`bot-suggest/ds-naming-apply/<branch>`, with a `refactor!:` commit and a
`BREAKING CHANGE` footer.

**Not done by the workflow yet:** renaming functions and test files,
reordering arguments, adding deprecated aliases for old names, harmonising
`@param` texts, and packages that call the renamed functions.

## Before you start

- **GitHub App:** installed on the client and the server repository, which
  must have the same owner, see [GitHub App](getting-started.qmd#github-app).
- **Claude access:** a federation rule for `ds-naming-check.yml`, see
  [Claude setup](claude-setup.qmd). With `max-claude-calls: 0` no Claude
  access is needed, and unclear arguments stay `unresolved`.
- **Adjusting the rules:** a file at the same path in your repository is
  merged over the shared one, see
  [adjusting the guidance](suggestions.qmd#adjusting-the-guidance).
